newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Britain, Irish minister to review N.Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Britain, Irish minister to review N.Ireland.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring and Britain's new Northern Ireland Secretary, Mo Mowlam, will review year-old Northern Ireland peace talks in Dublin on Thursday, officials said on Monday.
They said Mowlam, appointed when Britain's Labour party swept to power in May 1 elections, would meet Spring for informal talks, the first in Dublin since the poll.
The talks take place after both governments reversed a ban on contact with the Irish Republican Army's political wing, Sinn Fein, this month.

But both insist that Sinn Fein, which seeks to end British rule of Northern Ireland, cannot join peace talks which resume in Belfast on June 3 until there is a complete end to the guerrillas' violence.
The talks group the Irish nationalist SDLP party and pro-British Unionists, who want the province to remain British.
Thursday's meeting will be held on the day that U.S. President Bill Clinton meets British Prime Minister Tony Blair in London.
Clinton is expected to to reaffirm Washington's support for the two governments and their efforts to secure a new IRA truce to enable Sinn Fein to take part in the negotiations.
The IRA bombed London in February last year, ending a 17-month ceasefire that ushered in brief hopes of a peaceful settlement to a 28-year conflict that has killed 3,200.
